critical_blockers_detailed.title: SCHEMA DIVERGENCE - Assets Table: 72% Field Loss
critical_blockers_detailed.description: Monolith assets table contains 25 fields; ticket-service microservice retains only 7 fields (id, asset_tag, name, serial_number, location_id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at). 18 fields are completely absent.
critical_blockers_detailed.root_cause: Microservice designed for ticket-context asset lookup only; not full asset management
critical_blockers_detailed.impact: Data loss on import; ticket-service cannot support asset lifecycle features

resolution_options.title: Expand ticket-service assets schema
pros: All asset data available to ticket service
cons: Violates service boundary (ticket service shouldn't manage asset lifecycle)

resolution_options.title: Create separate asset-service microservice
pros: Enables asset queries from other services via API

resolution_options.title: Accept limited ticket-service scope
cons: Significant feature loss (warranty, supplier, division tracking)
Cannot link ticket to asset details

critical_blockers_detailed.recommendation: HALT IMPORT: Requires architectural decision. Recommend Option 2 (separate asset-service) for long-term microservices health.

critical_blockers_detailed.title: DUPLICATE NETWORK FIELDS: ip/ip_address and mac/mac_address
critical_blockers_detailed.description: Assets table contains both ip AND ip_address columns (both varchar 45), and both mac AND mac_address columns (both varchar 17). Data analysis shows only *_address versions are populated; ip and mac columns are NULL in all records.
evidence: CREATE TABLE assets shows both column definitions
Data dump shows only ip_address and mac_address contain values
ip and mac columns are NULL in all 234 asset records examined
critical_blockers_detailed.root_cause: Field refactoring without cleanup (likely added *_address versions, kept legacy names)
critical_blockers_detailed.impact: Migration must decide which to retain; ambiguous field mapping to microservice

resolution.action: Verify application code (Laravel models, controllers) to confirm it writes to *_address fields only
Confirm ip and mac columns are not used anywhere (search codebase for references)
Consolidate: Import only ip_address and mac_address to microservice
In post-migration cleanup: Remove ip and mac columns from monolith

critical_blockers_detailed.title: PRIMARY KEY TYPE MISMATCH: int(10) vs bigint
critical_blockers_detailed.description: Monolith uses int(10) UNSIGNED for primary keys; microservices use bigint UNSIGNED. Foreign key constraints will fail if types don't match during import.
critical_blockers_detailed.impact: Database import will fail with FK constraint violations; data corruption risk

resolution.action: During migration process, convert all int(10) UNSIGNED to bigint UNSIGNED
Update all FK columns to match new type
Verify data integrity post-conversion (no value overflow, no duplicate values)

Disable soft deletes in ticket-service microservice OR manually add deleted_at post-import
